bridge_checked: Sheaf-theoretic Witt groups / signature integrality / L-theory (Balmer, Woolf, Ranicki-Weiss, Verdier) used to prove Hilbert-Smith: integral character classes z_i on a test lattice fixed in advance, which a faithful Z_p action would split into p^k equal parts for every k. Sub-import: finite-group isotypic signature divisibility (Atiyah-Singer / Gilmer) applied to profinite Z_p with |G| = p^k unbounded.

closest_prior_work.ref: Atiyah-Singer, The index of elliptic operators III (G-signature theorem); Hirzebruch; Wall (topological case); Gilmer 1981 (isotypic signatures of branched covers)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: For a free action of a finite group G on a closed manifold, sign(g,M)=0 for g != 1. So the isotypic parts of the signature are equal and sign(M) = |G| sign(M/G), which makes |G| divide sign(M). Gilmer-style isotypic signatures split the form by characters. This is exactly 304's counting template, but for one finite group acting on a manifold with a manifold quotient. It is never run with |G| = p^k unbounded, against a profinite group or a wild orbit space.

closest_prior_work.ref: R. F. Williams, The construction of certain 0-dimensional groups (TAMS 129); A. Dranishnikov, On some problems related to the Hilbert-Smith conjecture (Sbornik 2016)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: This is the only prior attack on Hilbert-Smith found that uses a generalized-cohomology characteristic-class invariant on the p^k tower. It works with the K-theory of the lens spaces L(p^k) and the infinite cup product in K-theory of a rough B(Z_p), and plays unbounded growth against finite dimension. It covers only free actions with finite-dimensional orbit space and is conditional on two open problems. It uses no signatures, L-theory or Witt groups, and its contradiction is cup-length nilpotence, not lattice divisibility.

closest_prior_work.ref: C. T. Yang, p-adic transformation groups (Michigan Math. J. 7); Bredon-Raymond-Williams, p-adic groups of transformations (TAMS 99)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Uses the tower M/p^k Z_p -> M/Z_p of p-sheeted maps, transfers and p-power divisibility in the integral cohomology of the orbit space to show that the orbit space has dimension n+2. This is p-power divisibility of an invariant under the Z_p tower, but it yields dimension raising, not a contradiction. 304 explicitly contrasts its route with this one.

closest_prior_work.ref: Cappell-Shaneson-Weinberger, Classes topologiques caracteristiques pour les actions de groupes sur les espaces singuliers (C. R. Acad. Sci. 313); Rosenberg, The G-signature theorem revisited (1999); Banagl-Leichtnam-Piazza, The G-signature theorem on Witt spaces (arXiv 2511.21586)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Equivariant L-classes and G-signatures on singular or stratified spaces, for finite groups (CSW, Rosenberg) or compact Lie groups (BLP). This is the closest machinery: signature theory for group actions on non-manifold spaces. None of it treats profinite groups or Hilbert-Smith. The CSW note's text was not seen and is judged from its title and the program it belongs to.

closest_prior_work.ref: E. Shelukhin, A symplectic Hilbert-Smith conjecture
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Excludes Z_p actions by Hamiltonian homeomorphisms on symplectically aspherical manifolds, using barcodes and p-th power operations in Floer cohomology. A homological invariant with p-power structure gives a k-independent lower bound for p-power-order elements, which continuity contradicts. It uses a non-classical algebraic-topology invariant against Z_p, but no signatures or L-theory, and needs a symplectic hypothesis.

closest_prior_work.ref: Repovs-Scepin, A proof of the Hilbert-Smith conjecture for actions by Lipschitz maps (Math. Ann. 308)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Haar-averages an invariant metric so that the Hausdorff dimension of the orbit space stays at most n, which contradicts Yang's n+2. This is a fixed bound against forced growth and is the source of 304's averaging device, but the invariant is metric, not signature. Maleshich (Holder) and Martin (quasiconformal) follow the same metric/dimension line.

closest_prior_work.ref: Izumi; Gardella et al. (Rokhlin-property K-theory divisibility for finite/compact group actions on C*-algebras)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: A Rokhlin action of a finite group forces divisibility of K-theory by |G|. This has the same equal-parts-forces-divisibility shape in operator algebras. It was never applied to Hilbert-Smith; arXiv Rokhlin-dimension papers for compact groups never mention it.

closest_prior_work.ref: J. Pardon, The Hilbert-Smith conjecture for three-manifolds (JAMS 26)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Dimension 3 via incompressible surfaces and the induced action on a mapping class group. It is purely 3-manifold topology with no signature input.

closest_prior_work.ref: Ranicki-Weiss, On the construction and topological invariance of the Pontryagin classes (2010); Woolf, Witt groups of sheaves on topological spaces (2008)
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: These are the source of the imported machinery: local chain or sheaf L-theory and Witt groups over generated categories. 304 calls Ranicki-Weiss a 'close antecedent' for the category strategy. Neither mentions group actions or Hilbert-Smith.

closest_prior_work.ref: POST-RELEASE (not precedent): A. Dabrowski's AI agents, Integral tail signatures and the Hilbert-Smith conjecture, github.com/adbrw/HS_proof
closest_prior_work.what_it_does: Dated 2026-10-08, after the 2026-10-06 release. It runs a controlled-L-theory 'signature tail' argument: classes in L_4(A_G(T)) have signatures eventually divisible by p, while an effective Z_p action realizes tail 1. This is the same idea family as 304, but its authors are AI agents and it post-dates the release, so it may be derivative. Its README cites no prior signature approach to Hilbert-Smith.

what_is_new: Signature/Witt-group integrality has never before been aimed at Hilbert-Smith. The new move pairs a lattice fixed before k with p^k equal parts, and takes these parts from germ-localized character projectors on non-constructible sheaf categories over a test target, instead of from the wild orbit space. The underlying finite-group divisibility count, |G| divides the signature, is classical.

notes: Standard used: 'nothing even close'. (1) Main bridge, sheaf Witt/signature/L-theory to Hilbert-Smith: no pre-release work found that attacks Hilbert-Smith or Z_p actions with signatures, Witt groups, L-theory, surgery, assembly or Novikov-type invariants. That covers the arXiv corpus, Dranishnikov's 2016 survey of approaches, 304's own bibliography and introduction, and web search. The nearest Hilbert-Smith-specific invariant attack is the Williams/Dranishnikov K-theory programme, which differs in invariant, mechanism and scope; it is related, not close. (2) Sub-import, finite-group isotypic divisibility to profinite Z_p: the finite-group template (free G-action implies |G| divides sign) is classical and close to 304's counting step. It is not a bridge to Hilbert-Smith, and no prior work runs it with |G| = p^k unbounded against Z_p. The well-known obstacle, that M/p^kZ_p is not a manifold, is exactly what 304's test-sphere, fixed-lattice device gets around. (3) Calibration: if a strict reader treats 'finite-group signature divisibility exists' as 'close' to the bridge, the verdict for the sub-import becomes 'close precedent exists'. For the main Witt/L-theory-to-Hilbert-Smith bridge it stays 'novel'. (4) Confidence is held to 0.6 mainly because Weinberger 2011, CSW 1991 and Weinberger's books could not be read, MathOverflow and zbMATH were unreachable, and folklore remarks (e.g. 'signature arguments fail because orbit spaces are not manifolds') may exist in talks or unpublished notes. (5) Post-release: Dabrowski (2026-10-08) is a same-family L-theory 'signature tail' proof by AI agents. It is not a precedent and is relevant for contamination control. Coppola's audit independently describes 304's mechanism as 'not Yang dim-raising'.
